newsitem.title: USA: Freeport, IMC Global ink merger pact.
newsitem.headline: Freeport, IMC Global ink merger pact.

text.p: IMC Global Inc and Freeport-McMoRan Inc said Monday they reached non-binding agreement on a stock swap merger that would leave IMC Global as the surviving entity.

Under terms of the deal, IMC will swap 0.9 of a share plus one warrant for each Freeport-McMoRan share. The warrant will entitle holders to buy one-third of an IMC share at a price equal to $44.50 per share.

The deal would cement a long-standing relationship between the two companies. IMC Global and Freeport-McMoRan Resource Partners LP, Freeport's 51.6 percent owned unit, are already in a joint venture which makes them one of the largest integrated phosphate fertilizer producers in the world.
Besides their fertilizer operations, IMC Global and Freeport-McMoran together own an 83.3 percent stake in the Main Pass Block 299 sulphur and oil and gas operations.
IMC owns 25 percent of Main Pass 299 and Freeport-McMoRan Resource Partners LP unit holds 58.3 percent.

The merger calls for each company to contribute its Main Pass 299 stake to a newly-formed subsidiary of Freeport Resource Partners. Freeport Resource will also contribute its sulphur business to the new subsidiary, the companies said.
Shares in the as-yet-unnamed unit would then be distributed to all Freeport Resource shareholders.

Freeport-McMoRan said it would distribute shares it received in the new company directly to its shareholders. The companies said they would seek New York Stock Exchange listings for the new unit's shares, as well as the warrants to be issued by IMC Global.
Freeport-McMoRan said it expected annual general and administrative cash cost savings of at least $33 million from the deal, rising to $40 million in the next several years.

The companies said chairman James Moffett and Rene Latiolas, who is president and chief executive of both Freeport-McMoRan and Freeport Resource, will retire prior to the merger and accept board positions at IMC Global.
